$$D = \frac{P}{v} = \frac{24000}{20} = 1200\text{ N}$$

$$a = \frac{D - R}{m} = \frac{1200 - 450}{1200} = \frac{750}{1200} = 0.625\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Power driving force on level road: Show that the maximum speed V satisfies the equation 3V^2 + ...

hints: At maximum speed $V$, acceleration is zero, so $D = R$.
Substitute $D = \frac{36000}{V}$ and $R = 400 + 12V$ into $\frac{36000}{V} = 400 + 12V$.
Multiply through by $V$ and divide by common factor 4 to form the quadratic equation, then solve for positive root.

walkthrough.text:
At maximum speed $V$, acceleration is zero, so driving force equals resistance:
$$D = R \implies \frac{36000}{V} = 400 + 12V$$

Multiply throughout by $V$:
$$36000 = 400V + 12V^2 \implies 12V^2 + 400V - 36000 = 0$$
Divide through by 4:
$$3V^2 + 100V - 9000 = 0$$

Solve the quadratic equation using the quadratic formula:
$$V = \frac{-100 \pm \sqrt{100^2 - 4(3)(-9000)}}{2(3)} = \frac{-100 \pm \sqrt{10000 + 108000}}{6} = \frac{-100 \pm \sqrt{118000}}{6}$$
Since $V > 0$:
$$V = \frac{-100 + 343.51}{6} = \frac{243.51}{6} \approx 40.6\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Equate power to work rate against velocity-dependent resistance:
$$P = Rv \implies 36000 = (400 + 12V)V$$

Rearrange into standard quadratic form:
$$12V^2 + 400V - 36000 = 0 \implies 3V^2 + 100V - 9000 = 0$$

Extract positive physical root:
$$V = \frac{-100 + \sqrt{118000}}{6} \approx 40.6\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Equates $\frac{36000}{V} = 400 + 12V$ for dynamic equilibrium at maximum speed.
Correctly derives the quadratic equation $3V^2 + 100V - 9000 = 0$.
Solves quadratic equation to obtain $V = 40.6\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

Use $P_{\max} = D v_{\max}$ to calculate the driving force $D$ at $40\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Equate $D$ to $k(40^2)$ and solve for $k$.

walkthrough.text:
At maximum speed $v_{\max} = 40\text{ m s}^{-1}$, acceleration is zero, so the driving force equals resistance:
$$D = R$$
Calculate driving force from maximum power $P_{\max} = 120000\text{ W}$:
$$D = \frac{P_{\max}}{v_{\max}} = \frac{120000}{40} = 3000\text{ N}$$

Substitute $v = 40$ into the resistance model $R = kv^2$:
$$R = k(40^2) = 1600k$$

Equate driving force to resistance:
$$3000 = 1600k \implies k = \frac{3000}{1600} = \frac{15}{8} = 1.875$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Dynamic equilibrium at terminal velocity requires:
$$D = \frac{P_{\max}}{v_{\max}} = \frac{120000}{40} = 3000\text{ N}$$

Matching this force to the velocity-squared resistance law:
$$1600k = 3000 \implies k = 1.875$$

ai_rubric.observable: Calculates driving force at maximum speed $D = \frac{120000}{40} = 3000\text{ N}$.
Forms equilibrium equation $3000 = k(40^2)$.
Correctly deduces $k = 1.875$ (or $\frac{15}{8}$).

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Power driving force on level road: Find the acceleration of the truck when it is moving at 20\t...

hints: Find the resistance at $v = 20\text{ m s}^{-1}$ using $R = 1.875(20^2)$.
Find driving force at $v = 20\text{ m s}^{-1}$ using $D = \frac{120000}{20}$.
Apply Newton's second law: $D - R = ma$ with $m = 8000\text{ kg}$.
Solve for acceleration $a$.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the resistance at speed $v = 20\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$R = 1.875(20^2) = 1.875(400) = 750\text{ N}$$

Calculate driving force at $v = 20\text{ m s}^{-1}$ with power $P = 120000\text{ W}$:
$$D = \frac{P}{v} = \frac{120000}{20} = 6000\text{ N}$$

Apply Newton's second law to find acceleration:
$$D - R = ma \implies 6000 - 750 = 8000a \implies 5250 = 8000a \implies a = \frac{5250}{8000} = 0.65625\text{ m s}^{-2} \approx 0.656\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
At half terminal velocity, resistance is one-fourth of its terminal value:
$$R = 1.875(400) = 750\text{ N}$$

Driving force is doubled compared to maximum speed:
$$D = \frac{120000}{20} = 6000\text{ N}$$

Acceleration is determined by net tractive force:
$$a = \frac{6000 - 750}{8000} = \frac{5250}{8000} = 0.65625\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Calculates resistance $R = 1.875(20^2) = 750\text{ N}$.
Finds driving force $D = \frac{120000}{20} = 6000\text{ N}$ and sets up $6000 - 750 = 8000a$.
Obtains acceleration $a = 0.656\text{ m s}^{-2}$ (or $0.65625\text{ m s}^{-2}$).

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Power driving force on level road: Find the power required to maintain a steady speed of 30\tex...

hints: At steady speed $30\text{ m s}^{-1}$, $D = R = 1.875(30^2) = 1687.5\text{ N}$.
Power needed for steady speed is $P = Dv = 1687.5(30)$.
At maximum power ($120\text{ kW}$), new driving force is $D_{\text{max}} = \frac{120000}{30} = 4000\text{ N}$.
Use $D_{\text{max}} - 1687.5 = 8000a$ to find the instantaneous acceleration.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate resistance at steady speed $v = 30\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$R = 1.875(30^2) = 1.875(900) = 1687.5\text{ N}$$
To maintain steady speed, $D = R = 1687.5\text{ N}$. The required power is:
$$P = Dv = 1687.5(30) = 50625\text{ W} = 50.625\text{ kW}$$

When power is increased to maximum ($P_{\max} = 120000\text{ W}$) at $v = 30\text{ m s}^{-1}$, the new driving force is:
$$D_{\text{new}} = \frac{120000}{30} = 4000\text{ N}$$

Apply Newton's second law to find the instantaneous acceleration:
$$D_{\text{new}} - R = ma \implies 4000 - 1687.5 = 8000a \implies 2312.5 = 8000a$$
$$a = \frac{2312.5}{8000} = 0.2890625\text{ m s}^{-2} \approx 0.289\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Power required to overcome air resistance at steady $30\text{ m s}^{-1}$ is:
$$P = R v = 1.875(30^3) = 50625\text{ W} = 50.625\text{ kW}$$

Under maximum engine power ($120\text{ kW}$), available tractive force is $4000\text{ N}$:
$$a = \frac{4000 - 1687.5}{8000} = \frac{2312.5}{8000} \approx 0.289\text{ m s}^{-2}$$
